thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 DNS anomaly: high DNS error-rate and truncated responses for api.redwood-inference.com from multiple EU resolvers (detected by probe-runner). Pager: @tom-oncall. Channel: #incident-3412400000.

rachel: CS flagged multiple tickets at 09:41 UTC — customers in NL and DE seeing 502/504 and some SDKs failing with "no such host" intermittently. Can repro from an ISP in Amsterdam (curl errors).

anna-sre: confirmed via probes: spike in SERVFAIL and EDNS truncation UDP->TCP fallbacks. A distinct subset of Cloudflare resolver IPs in eu cluster are consistently returning truncated UDP packets leading to retries and timeouts. Noticed after an automatic geo-shift at 08:55 UTC.

jorge-net: grabbing our GeoDNS controller audit logs. The geo controller performed an auto-rebalancing step at 08:55:34 UTC shifting 35% traffic toward eu-west-1 primary due to capacity signals. No manual DNS edits.

meera-cs: CS needs wording for status. Any quick ETA?

anna-sre: triage plan: 1) minimize client exposure by shifting DNS weights away from impacted eu cluster 2) add a short-lived ALIAS/ANAME to Anycast frontends with TTL=20s 3) run targeted TCP-only checks to see if resolvers respond correctly over TCP 4) open Cloudflare & AWS tickets with full pcaps. I'll coordinate with tom for the push.

incident-bot: queued actions: assign -> tom-oncall.

tom-oncall: executing mitigation now: (a) pause geo-autoscaler (b) set eu-west-1 weight -> 10% (c) create ALIAS fallback to anycast-edge (d) enable stricter health-check gating for weight changes. Pushing changes.

incident-bot: change recorded: autoscaler paused (09:49 UTC). Audit: https://internal/geo/audit/3412400000

anna-sre: pushed ALIAS fallback and lowered eu-west-1 weight. Monitoring probes.

jorge-net: started collecting DNS pcaps and resolver lists. Observed that some CF resolvers are returning EDNS0 OPT with unusual size causing truncation; suspect MTU/fragmentation path issue between CF cluster and upstream.

cf-support-bot: Cloudflare ticket opened CF-2026-4001. Please attach your pcap + dig traces.

rachel: publishing customer note: status.redwood-inference.com/incidents/3412400000 -> "Degraded service: intermittent DNS resolution failures affecting EU customers. Mitigation in progress." ETA 30m.

meera-cs: sending targeted messages to 8 impacted enterprise customers with manual retry guidance and request to confirm recovery after 1-2 minutes.

anna-sre: quick test after fallback: many clients that hit Anycast frontends succeed, overall EU error-rate dropped from 5.7% -> 0.9%. But there's a residual cohort still cached to bad resolvers. We're seeing successful TCP queries while UDP occasionally truncates.

tom-oncall: next actions: 1) request CF to warm TCP paths / confirm resolver health 2) keep ALIAS fallback for 45m 3) add resolver health metric to dashboards 4) review autoscaler step size to avoid single-shift spikes.

anna-sre: capturing example traces:
```
# dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood-inference.com A +bufsize=512 +short
;; -> sometimes returns nothing
# dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood-inference.com A +tcp +short
52.210.12.34 13.35.99.12
# tcpdump -n -s0 -w dns.pcap port 53
(see attachment in #incident-3412400000)
```

jorge-net: preliminary root-cause hypothesis: path MTU or EDNS buffer mismatch between CF recursive cluster and our authoritative responses is triggering truncation and unreliable UDP behavior; autoscaler suddenly shifted clients to that cluster amplifying visibility. Need CF to validate their egress path.

cf-support-bot: CF acknowledged ticket CF-2026-4001 and requested pcaps and timestamps 09:30-09:55 UTC. They escalated to resolver engineering.

meera-cs: customers reporting mixed statuses; most show recovery after 20-90s due to cache TTL, a few report persistent failures and we've provided immediate routing overrides.

anna-sre: mitigation scoreboard:
- autoscaler paused (09:49)
- eu-west-1 weight reduced to 10% (09:50)
- ALIAS fallback to Anycast frontends created (09:51)
- TCP-only probe run and pcaps collected (09:52)
- CF ticket CF-2026-4001 opened (09:54)
- AWS support ticket AWS-rtb-400002 opened (09:55)

jorge-net: also noticed that our authoritative response set had mixed RRSIG sizes (DNSSEC) which increases packet size; as a quick improvement we're going to temporarily shorten some TXT metadata so responses fit smaller UDP frames. Pushing a low-risk tweak now.

rachel: CS note: severity escalated to sev2. ETA for next update 30m. Posting to status page and sending in-app banner to affected customers.

tom-oncall: scheduled handoff to anna-sre in 40m if unresolved. If CF confirms fix earlier we'll unwind fallbacks and restore autoscaler.

anna-sre: follow-ups for postmortem: 1) autoscaler backoff + DNS success gating 2) add resolver-path MTU/EDNS checks in probe runner 3) add DNS TCP health as a first-class metric 4) docs for CS on DNS caching expectations and guidance. Filing GH issues: https://git.internal/infra/geo-dns/issues/212 and https://git.internal/infra/observability/issues/98.

cf-support-bot: Cloudflare notes: engineering investigating EDNS truncation behavior in EU resolver cluster and will provide timeline within 30m.

meera-cs: targeted follow-up messages queued to impacted enterprises with reference to incident 3412400000.

anna-sre: stats at 10:03 UTC: EU error-rate ~0.6%. Residual errors attributed to ISP caches holding SERVFAILs; expect to fully normalize within 5-10 minutes after caches expire.

incident-bot: incident state -> monitoring/mitigation. Last update: 10:03 UTC. Tags: [dns, geodns, cloudflare, route53, edns, production].

rachel: will consolidate logs and handoff notes for the post-incident writeup. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
